entries.title: How can you count syllables in a word?
entries.answer: A syllable is one sound part of a spoken word. Say rainbow slowly and listen for two parts, rain and bow. If you clap once on each part, you clap twice. Frog has one syllable and dinosaur has three. A syllable usually has a vowel sound that you can hear, such as the long a sound in rain. Counting letters on the page will not tell you how many syllables you said. A word like cake has four letters but just one syllable.
facts: A spoken word can have one syllable or several syllables.
Different accents can change the number of syllables a speaker says in some words.

entries.title: How did the Rosetta Stone help people read hieroglyphs?
entries.answer: The Rosetta Stone has the same announcement carved in three kinds of writing. One is in Greek, which scholars could already read. The other two use ancient Egyptian scripts, called hieroglyphs and Demotic. Comparing the parts gave scholars clues to the Egyptian signs. A royal name, for example, could help them make a guess about which signs represented its sounds. The stone is only part of a larger slab. Much of its upper section is missing, so there were gaps to work around.

sections.heading: A long puzzle
sections.text: In 1822, Jean-François Champollion announced a breakthrough in reading hieroglyphs. He built on work by several scholars, including Thomas Young.

facts: The announcement was made in 196 BCE.
The stone uses three scripts to write two languages.

entries.title: How do Egyptian hieroglyphs work?
entries.answer: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs are signs used to write the Egyptian language. Some are easy to recognize as pictures, such as an owl or an eye. Their job still depends on where they appear in the writing. One sign can stand for a sound. Another can stand for a whole word. Some give a reader a clue about what kind of word appears nearby. A reader therefore needs to know the writing system to understand a line of signs, just as reading English takes more than recognizing a letter’s shape.
facts: In Egyptian hieroglyphs, an owl sign can represent the sound m.
Hieroglyphs appear in carved and painted inscriptions.

entries.title: How do people read braille?
entries.answer: Braille uses patterns of raised dots. A reader feels them with their fingertips. In six-dot braille, each space, called a cell, has room for six dots arranged in two columns. Which dots stick up tells the reader what the pattern means. Braille can represent letters, numbers, and other signs. In some versions, one pattern can stand for a whole word or a group of letters to save space. People use braille to read books, label things, and find their way around buildings.

sections.heading: Who invented it?
sections.text: Louis Braille developed the system as a young student in France. Before braille, some blind students learned to feel the shapes of raised print letters.

facts: A standard braille cell has room for six dots.
Braille is a way of writing and reading a language.

entries.title: How does American Sign Language work?
entries.answer: American Sign Language, or ASL, is a language that people can see. Signers use their hands, faces, and bodies to express ideas. A change in where or how a sign moves can matter, much as a change in sound can matter in a spoken language. ASL has its own grammar, the patterns people use to put ideas together. Some signs may look a little like what they mean, but people need to learn the language to understand a conversation.

sections.heading: Many sign languages
sections.text: ASL is used by many people in the United States and parts of Canada. British Sign Language is different, even though many hearing people in both places speak English.

facts: ASL is a natural language with rules of its own.
Signers can use their face and body to help express a question or idea.

entries.title: What is an alphabet?
entries.answer: An alphabet is a set of letters used to write a language. In an alphabet, letters or groups of letters stand for sounds. This gives a writer a way to spell many words with a small set of signs. English uses 26 letters. The spelling does not always tell you which sound to make. In the word ship, for instance, s and h together stand for one sound. Other writing systems organize signs differently, and languages using the same alphabet can give its letters different jobs.
facts: English uses a form of the Latin alphabet.
A letter is a written mark. A sound is something you can say or hear.

entries.title: Why did people press signs into clay?
entries.answer: In ancient Mesopotamia, people used clay tablets as writing surfaces. A writer used a tool called a stylus to press small wedge shapes into soft clay. Groups of wedges formed signs in a system called cuneiform. Keeping track of food and other goods was one early use. People also wrote letters, stories, and math on tablets. A clay tablet could dry and become hard, allowing some messages to last for thousands of years. The marks often survive even when part of the tablet breaks.
facts: The earliest clay records used picture-like signs before wedge-shaped signs became common.
Ancient writers used cuneiform to record several languages, including Sumerian and Akkadian.
